title: finding(fields): `dueLike` is declared for "date/datetime" fields but `DateTimeCellRenderer` never reads it — the overdue affordance is silently dropped on a `datetime` column
body:
Found while implementing objectui#8853 (the `field.format` vocabulary split between the same two cell renderers) by the objectui `domain:ui` seat, session `session_01MPaVWWMuWeT5LgB1qoXjVB`. Filed rather than fixed there: it is a DIFFERENT authored key with its own design call (should a `datetime` cell paint overdue at all?), and #8853's ruling is scoped to `field.format`. Not claimed, no code written for this one.

## The declared contract

`packages/types/src/zod/views.zod.ts`, `DetailViewFieldSchema`, the `dueLike` member's own `describe` text, quoted verbatim:

> Marks a date/datetime field as due/deadline-semantic, gating the relative "Overdue Nd" wording (vs. neutral "Nd ago" for start/end/created dates)

"date/datetime". Both types, in the schema description an author reads.

## What the runtime does

- `packages/types/src/field-types.ts` declares `dueLike?: boolean` on `DateFieldMetadata` only. `DateTimeFieldMetadata` next to it does not carry it.
- `packages/fields/src/index.tsx`: `DateCellRenderer` reads it (the `dueLike` const, the `isOverdue` const, the red class). `DateTimeCellRenderer` does not mention it — zero occurrences in that function.

## Measured

`TZ=UTC` (pinned by the root vitest config), `en-US`, clock pinned to `2026-09-09T12:00:00.000Z`, value `2026-09-06T09:30:00.000Z` (3 days past, inside the plus-or-minus 7-day relative window), rendered through the two cell renderers directly:

| field | rendered text | rendered span class |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `date`, `dueLike: true`, `format: 'relative'` | `Overdue 3d` | `tabular-nums text-red-600` |
| `datetime`, `dueLike: true`, `format: 'relative'` | `3 days ago` | `tabular-nums text-sm whitespace-nowrap` |
| `datetime`, no `dueLike`, `format: 'relative'` | `3 days ago` | `tabular-nums text-sm whitespace-nowrap` |

Rows 2 and 3 are byte-identical: the authored key changes nothing. Same silent-drop signature as objectui#8853 and objectui#8352 — the runtime accepts the key, parses it, drops it, and renders something that still looks like a legitimate relative date, so a reader cannot tell an honoured `dueLike` from a dropped one by looking at the cell.

## Why it is worth a card now rather than before

Before objectui#8853's fix this was unreachable in practice: the `datetime` cell had no relative face at all, so `dueLike` had nothing to gate. That fix makes `format: 'relative'` resolve on a `datetime` cell, so the relative face is now live there and `dueLike` is now an authored key sitting next to a face it visibly fails to change. #8853 deliberately did NOT thread it — acquiring a second key's behaviour while honouring the first would be an unruled change, and the "Overdue Nd" wording travels with red styling and a field-name heuristic, not just a word.

## The decision this needs

Not a threading slip — a real call, which is why it is filed rather than guessed:

1. Thread `dueLike` (and the field-name heuristic, and the red styling) into `DateTimeCellRenderer`, so one authored key means one thing across the two cells. Costs: a new visual affordance on `datetime` columns that never had it.
2. Narrow the `describe` text to "date field", making the schema honest about what is implemented, and leave the renderer alone.

Option 1 is the shape objectui#8352 and objectui#8853 both took for their key; option 2 is the enforce-or-remove direction. Either closes the gap; shipping neither leaves an authored key whose documentation names a type the runtime ignores.

## Scope note

⛔ Not the same as objectui#8853 (that one is `field.format`, already ruled and implemented). ⛔ Not objectui#8263 (`formatMeasureDate` in `packages/core`, a different file and package). Dedupe: one targeted search over the `dueLike` / overdue / datetime vocabulary returned 0 results; the run carried a lit control on the same channel in the same session (a near-verbatim title query that returned objectui#8853 itself), so the zero is a reading rather than a dead query.
